scenarios.outcome: The sequence is understandable, but no public artifact defines the required command/interface for preparing manifests, recording unsupported capability, consolidating findings, or generating the final readiness report.

scenarios.steps: Encounter repeated normalized failures during the gauntlet.
scenarios.outcome: Escalation is required, but assumption review or model escalation does not identify the decision-maker, required recorded artifact, or precise resume state.

findings.summary: Unsupported-host handling says an external agent or maintainer supplies missing roles, but does not specify who is authorized to unblock, how reports are submitted/bound, or which status transition makes completion legal.
Repeated-failure escalation lacks an owner, required evidence/decision record, and deterministic state transition, so agents can reasonably implement incompatible recovery behavior.
Final readiness report is required but has no defined public schema, location, authoring command, or exact unresolved conditions beyond examples.
The role staging/binding workflow names commands and manifests but does not define how an unsupported-host disclosure is represented in the Work Item/PR or how that disclosure is validated.

residualRisks: Agents may leave unsupported-host work permanently stalled or incorrectly self-unblock it.
Different implementations may record escalation and readiness state inconsistently.
A mechanically valid report could be treated as sufficient without a clearly specified authority and status transition.
